scat_fig1_beam_ring.png: A horizontal axis runs to a scattering center marked by a dot. Two kinds of line are distinguished in the drawing only by colour, so they are named here: the particle's path is the continuous blue curve, while the axis and a pair of closely spaced straight lines running from the center up to the right are black. That black pair brackets the narrow interval of directions between theta and theta plus d theta. The blue path enters from the left parallel to the axis, offset above it by a height marked s between two arrowheads; a narrow, pointed lens shape around the entering beam, with a cusp where its two curves meet at top and bottom, marks the ring of incident particles, labelled as having area 2 pi s ds. The path stays straight until the apsidal point, a labelled dot above the axis, which is joined to the center by a short segment marked r with the subscript less-than, r sub less-than. Past that point the path turns up and to the right. The angle theta is marked between the lower black bracketing line and the forward axis. At the right a narrow hatched band curves the full height of the figure, standing for the ring of directions into which the particles emerge. A double-headed arrow sits between the text naming the particles incident with impact parameter between s and s plus ds and that band, touching neither; just below it a second double-headed arrow carries the label s and theta, stating that each impact parameter corresponds to one scattering angle. Three lines of equations sit at the upper left, a fourth sits above the axis near the apsidal-point label, and the heading INCIDENT INTENSITY sits at the lower left; all of them are set as text in the surrounding document.
scat_fig2_repulsive.png: Repulsive deflection, under the heading REPULSIVE CASE set at the top of the frame. A curved particle path arrives from the left just above a horizontal baseline, carries an arrowhead, and bends away from the center, leaving up and to the right; a separate straight line from the center marks the outgoing asymptote that the path approaches. A steep straight line, the apsidal line, runs from the upper left down through the turning point of the path to a vertex on the baseline, and the short segment marked along it is the distance of closest approach; the turning point above is labelled as the apsidal point. Two equal angles, both marked psi, share that vertex on the baseline and are measured from the apsidal line, one back to the incoming direction and one forward to the outgoing asymptote. The angle between the outgoing asymptote and the forward baseline is marked theta, further to the right. Alongside are the relations pi equals theta plus 2 psi; theta equals pi minus 2 psi; and psi equals, pi minus theta, all over two.
scat_fig3_attractive.png: Attractive deflection. A particle path arrives from the left above a horizontal baseline carrying an arrowhead and is pulled toward the center rather than pushed away, crossing the baseline at the vertex and continuing downward and to the right, still carrying the arrowhead. A steep straight line runs from the upper right down through the apsidal point, which is labelled at the upper right, and continues to that same vertex on the baseline: this is the apsidal line. Two angles marked psi share the vertex, one above the baseline opening back toward the incoming direction and one below it opening toward the outgoing asymptote. The deflection angle theta is marked lower right, between the outgoing asymptote and the forward baseline direction. Alongside are the relations pi equals 2 psi minus theta; theta equals 2 psi minus pi; and psi equals, pi plus theta, all over two.
scat_fig0_charges.png: Two small circles stand for point charges, the left one labelled Z e and the right one labelled Z prime e, set a short distance apart on a diagonal. Each carries a short arrow pointing away from the other along the line joining them, the left charge driven up and to the left and the right charge down and to the right, indicating that the two repel one another.
scat_fig4_scattering_center.png: A horizontal baseline with a dot at its middle marks the scattering center, labelled beneath it. A short beam arrow at the far left travels parallel to the baseline, offset above it by a height marked s between two arrowheads. A wide arc sweeps over the top from just above the baseline left of the center round to just above the baseline to its right, carrying an arrowhead at each end, and is labelled with the range 0 less than theta, theta at most pi, showing that every deflection direction from forward to backward, including exact backscattering, is available. A straight line runs up and to the right from the center as one such outgoing direction, and a plain arc with a rounded terminus at each end, not an arrowhead, runs from the baseline to that line to mark the angle theta between them.
